title: Beyond the 956: South Carolina father charged with attempted murder after 11-month-old found alive buried in dog crate
excerpt: Michael Comer, 25, was arrested in South Carolina after his 11-month-old son was found alive Tuesday, buried about a foot underground in a dog crate wrapped in a towel. The baby was rescued after nearly 24 hours underground and is expected to make a full recovery.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

An 11-month-old boy was found alive Tuesday, November 10, 2026, buried about a foot underground in a dog crate in a wooded area near Batesburg-Leesville, South Carolina, after nearly 24 hours underground, authorities said. His father, Michael Comer, 25, of Gaston, has been charged with attempted murder, unlawful conduct toward a child, custodial interference and burglary, according to arrest warrants cited by the Lexington County Sheriff's Department.

Nearly 100 first responders searched for the baby after he was reported missing Monday, November 9. Searchers spotted freshly disturbed dirt covered in pine straw off the 300 block of Parthenon Road and began digging. Officers heard the baby crying inside the crate, which was wrapped in a towel and measured about two feet by two feet, Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said.

Koon said the towel likely created a small pocket of air, and cold overnight weather may have slowed the baby's breathing, giving rescuers more time. The baby was found at about 1:30 p.m. Tuesday and rushed to a hospital. He was released Tuesday night and is with family members, and doctors expect him to make a full recovery, the sheriff's office said.

Comer was arrested Monday night in Batesburg-Leesville on charges of burglary and resisting arrest while the baby was still missing, authorities said. He was denied bond on the burglary charge and is being held in the Lexington County Detention Center. A bond hearing was scheduled for Thursday, November 12.

The charges are allegations. Comer is presumed innocent until proven guilty in court.

Update — November 12, 2026

A judge denied bond for Michael Comer on Thursday, November 12, The Associated Press reported. Lead investigator Tyler Douglas of the Lexington County Sheriff's Department told Judge Gary W. Reinhart that Comer showed no remorse for attempting to kill his son and tried to leave the state, according to the AP. Reinhart approved a public defender for Comer and set a hearing for December 10. CNN reported, citing South Carolina court records, that Comer pleaded guilty earlier this year to charges including assault and battery and domestic violence. Comer remains in custody in the Lexington County Detention Center.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post, Nov. 11, 2026; USA Today; CNN; The Associated Press (WIS), Nov. 12, 2026.
